lead: you found out you were his reference when the call came, and you had known for six years which way he goes when a thing gets hard, and you gave him the warm sentence anyway.
sun: membership was never the question — subs paid, invitations, your face in the photograph on the wall — and every year of it has been spent a pace off, which is the seat the sorting works from. by the second season you had them separated: the ones doing the thing and the ones attending it. that separation has not moved since, has never been said out loud, and is exact.
moon: nothing in you was ever occupied by a claim of your own, so your name goes into other people's arrangements without a conversation first. you learn you vouched for someone when the letter is acknowledged. The Empty District gets furnished on assumption — by the time any of it arrives it is already a fact, already thanked for, and already spent.
pull: your word goes out at full value on people you sorted years ago, and you were not in the room for a single one of those arrangements.
tension: nobody who uses your name has had to ask for it, which is why the warmth attached to you carries a faint surprise in it. an ask can be refused. an assumption cannot, and it cannot be corrected afterwards without the correction landing as a man being dropped by the person who had already backed him. the separation you made stays where it is, and your name keeps arriving in places you did not send it.
cost: strangers treat your read of a person as settled and act on it — a flat, a job, a place on somebody's crew — because it comes without hedging and it is usually right. which people it moves is decided by whoever picked your name up. the accuracy holds, it is in constant use, and the list it comes off has never been consulted.

lead: the drive home is twenty minutes and you spend it with the evening in two pieces on the seat beside you: the shape of the table, and the actual condition of everybody who was at it.
sun: you belong to that table in the flat sense — invited, expected, missed when absent — while sitting a pace off it, where the shape shows. The Flock takes the room apart while the room is being polite: the ones keeping it going, the ones for whom leaving would cost more than turning up. that division was complete before the plates were cleared, done from a position rather than a mood, and it holds.
moon: the whole of what that room is actually saying arrives as well, at the volume of the words themselves, with no setting between on and off. so you drive away holding the true condition of every person there alongside the diagram of them — one thing taken from where you sit, one delivered whether or not you had room for it, and the second is the one that empties you.
pull: you leave with the diagram and the weather both. the group thanks you for being observant, which credits the half that was free and cannot see the half that took all night.
tension: you get asked because you always know where everything is, and it is meant kindly, and it describes a night of work as a personality trait. the structural half really is free — the read takes a minute from where you sit — so the sentence is unarguable. the rest goes on all evening, arrives unasked, gets set down alone in a car, and any account of that from you would come out sounding like a boast about being perceptive.
cost: most of what a group is happens between what a room decides and what the room means, and both of those reach you on the same night, complete, without anybody arranging it. nobody who was there is short of anything afterwards. the work done in the corner of that evening has no name at the table, and being quick is the only part of it that gets credited.

lead: nobody in the boat can see the boat. you sit at the one end facing forward, calling a number, and the whole winter runs at whatever number you call.
sun: the crew is on one roll with you — same club, same subs, same photograph in the bar — and you sit inside it doing the one job nobody else in it does, at the only seat with all of them in view. from there it comes apart every outing: the pair actually moving the boat, and the ones whose blades are matching the pair. from the bank it reads as one body.
moon: what you have instead of a sentence is a rate. you put the number out, they come to it, the boat gets long and quiet, and nothing you saw passes between anybody. The Drum will not carry a comment, only a count — so the difference between the two halves of that crew sits buried inside a tempo everyone can meet, and the weaker end never has to find out.
pull: one count leaves your seat and the boat comes back as one animal. you are the only person in it who knows there are two crews, and the number is what keeps that from surfacing.
tension: moving a seat would mean saying out loud who is moving the boat and who is riding it, in a squad where everybody trains the same hours and the effort is assumed to be even. the number you call keeps flattering the half that needs it, and it works, which is what holds it in place. what you get called for that is reliable, which is a word about attendance, not about the arithmetic you are running in public.
cost: rowing above themselves, for a whole season, gets credited to the boat — true in a way that has you nowhere in it. the rate is doing the work of a conversation nobody in that crew would survive. a fortnight off and the timing goes, and they put it down to a bad patch rather than to the difference the number has been covering all season.

lead: the list for a saturday takes ten minutes and there is a decision on every line: one from this end, one from that end, of a group that has been two things since before anybody else worked it out.
sun: you have been in it long enough to be part of the fittings, and you have watched it come apart from the inside for years with no argument to date it by. the split is not in anybody's grievance. it is in what people turn up for, and the two ends have been running on separate reasons since one winter, which neither has had occasion to discover, because both of them keep meeting at yours.
moon: making room here is deliberate and dated: an evening chosen, an invitation said out loud, a table laid for people who would not otherwise be in one house at the same hour. what gets held in that space binds — The Void does not do casual — so a group's continued life as one thing has a venue, a night of the week, and one person quietly deciding the mix.
pull: they believe it is one thing on the evidence of your saturdays. you built that evidence on purpose, out of a seam you could see clearly and chose to lay a table over.
tension: the one who holds it all together gets said at the door, fondly, by people describing an evening rather than a repair. what cannot come out at that table is that the invitation is doing structural work — say it, and the night turns into an intervention, and the ones who came to relax find they were exhibits. so the sorting has to keep going out as hospitality, which is the one form of it nobody has to answer.
cost: people who have run out of reasons for each other spend a good evening in one room, several times a year, at your invitation, and go home with the impression that the thing is in decent health. the season you stop putting the evening on, the two ends find out about each other inside a few months, and the coming-apart gets dated to your stopping.
